arxiv-2012-12332.title: Ultraholomorphic sectorial extensions of Beurling type Thanks: AR was supported by FWF-Project P 32905-N, DNN and GS by FWF-Project P 33417-N
arxiv-2012-12332.creator: David Nicolas Nenning, Armin Rainer, and Gerhard Schindl
arxiv-2012-12332.description: Abstract . We prove sectorial extension theorems for ultraholomorphic function classes of Beurling type defined by weight functions with a controlled loss of regularity. The proofs are based on a reduction lemma, due to the second author, which allows to extract the Beurling from the Roumieu case, which was treated recently by Jiménez-Garrido, Sanz, and the third author.

arxiv-2109-10379.title: Scaling laws and a general theory for the growth of public companies
arxiv-2109-10379.creator: Jiang Zhang, Christopher P. Kempes, Marcus J. Hamilton, Ruyi Tao, Geoffrey B. West
arxiv-2109-10379.description: Abstract Publicly traded companies are fundamental units of contemporary economies and markets and are important mechanisms through which humans interact with their environments. Understanding the general properties that underlie the processes of their growth has long been of interest, yet fundamental debates about the effects of firm size on growth have persisted.

arxiv-2110-00633.title: Uniform Bounds for Scheduling with Job Size Estimates
arxiv-2110-00633.creator: Ziv Scully, Isaac Grosof, Michael Mitzenmacher
arxiv-2110-00633.description: Abstract We consider the problem of scheduling to minimize mean response time in M/G/1 queues where only estimated job sizes (processing times) are known to the scheduler, where a job of true size s s has estimated size in the interval [ β ​ s , α ​ s ] [\beta s,\alpha s] for some α ≥ β > 0

arxiv-2110-08747.title: JEL ratio test for independence of time to failure and cause of failure in competing risks Thanks: † Corresponding E-mail: sreedeviep@gmail.com
arxiv-2110-08747.creator: Sreelakshmy N. a and Sreedevi E. P. b a Prajyothi Nikethan College, Pudukkad, India. b SNGS College, Pattambi, India
arxiv-2110-08747.description: Abstract . In the present article, we propose jackknife empirical likelihood (JEL) ratio test for testing the independence of time to failure and cause of failure in competing risks data. We use U-statistic theory to derive the JEL ratio test. The asymptotic distribution of the test statistic is shown to be chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom.

arxiv-2203-12628.title: The dark side of the proton arXiv: 2203.xxxxx
arxiv-2203-12628.creator: Matthew McCullough, James Moore, Maria Ubiali
arxiv-2203-12628.description: Abstract We study the sensitivity of the High-Luminosity LHC to a light baryonic dark photon B B , primarily coupled to quarks, as a constituent of the proton. This is achieved by allowing for a dark photon parton distribution function (PDF) in the PDF evolution equations.

arxiv-2308-14930.title: Application of Quantum Pre-Processing Filter for Binary Image Classification with Small Samples
arxiv-2308-14930.description: Abstract Over the past few years, there has been significant interest in Quantum Machine Learning (QML) among researchers, as it has the potential to transform the field of machine learning. Several models that exploit the properties of quantum mechanics have been developed for practical applications.

arxiv-2312-05058.title: Spatial and Temporal Hierarchy for Autonomous Navigation using Active Inference in Minigrid Environment
arxiv-2312-05058.creator: Daria de Tinguy, Toon Van de Maele, Tim Verbelen, Bart Dhoedt
arxiv-2312-05058.description: Abstract Robust evidence suggests that humans explore their environment using a combination of topological landmarks and coarse grained path-integration. This approach relies on identifiable environmental features (topological landmarks) in tandem with estimations of distance and direction (coarse grained path-integration) to construct cognitive maps of the surroundings.

arxiv-2403-19384.title: Impact of JLab data on the determination of GPDs at zero skewness and new insights from transition form factors N → Δ N\rightarrow\Delta
arxiv-2403-19384.creator: The MMGPDs Collaboration: Muhammad Goharipour 1,2, Hadi Hashamipour 2, Fatemeh Irani 1, K. Azizi 1,2,3
arxiv-2403-19384.description: Abstract It is well established now that the generalized parton distributions (GPDs) at zero skewness are playing important roles in some physical process such as elastic electron-nucleon scattering, elastic (anti)neutrino-nucleon scattering, and wide-angle Compton scattering (WACS) via various types of form factors (FFs).

arxiv-2404-13095.title: Gaussian Process Approach for Model-Independent Reconstruction of f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) Gravity with Direct Hubble Measurements
arxiv-2404-13095.creator: Gaurav N. Gadbail, Sanjay Mandal, P.K. Sahoo
arxiv-2404-13095.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gaurav N. Gadbail, Sanjay Mandal, P.K. Sahoo. The increase of discrepancy in the standard procedure to choose the arbitrary functional form of the Lagrangian f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) motivates us to solve this issue in modified theories of gravity. In this regard, we investigate the Gaussian process (GP), which allows us to eliminate this issue in a f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) model-independent way.

arxiv-2410-21978.title: Data-driven approach for modeling the temporal and spectral evolution of kilonova systematic uncertainties
arxiv-2410-21978.creator: Sahil Jhawar, Thibeau Wouters, Peter T. H. Pang, Mattia Bulla, Michael W. Coughlin, Tim Dietrich
arxiv-2410-21978.description: Abstract Kilonovae, possible electromagnetic counterparts to neutron star mergers, provide important information about high-energy transient phenomena and, in principle, also allow us to obtain information about the source properties responsible for powering the kilonova. Unfortunately, numerous uncertainties exist in kilonova modeling that, at the current stage, hinder accurate predictions.

arxiv-2501-10551.title: An Empirical Study to Understand How Students Use ChatGPT for Writing Essays
arxiv-2501-10551.creator: Andrew Jelson, Daniel Manesh, Alice Jang, Daniel Dunlap, Young-Ho Kim, Sang Won Lee
arxiv-2501-10551.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrew Jelson, Daniel Manesh, Alice Jang, Daniel Dunlap, Young-Ho Kim, Sang Won Lee. As large language models (LLMs) become widespread, students increasingly turn to systems like ChatGPT for writing tasks. Educators worry that this reliance may reduce critical engagement with writing and hinder students’ learning processes. Although datasets exist on students’ use of LLMs for writing, how they functionally use ChatGPT in detail—and how this usage shapes their writing and perceptions—remains underexplored.

arxiv-2505-13653.title: UGC 10043 in depth: Dissecting the polar bulge and subtle low surface brightness features
arxiv-2505-13653.creator: S. K. H. Bahr & A. V. Mosenkov
arxiv-2505-13653.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S. K. H. Bahr & A. V. Mosenkov. Galaxies with polar structures (of which polar-ring galaxies (PRGs) are a prominent subclass) contain components that are kinematically decoupled and highly inclined relative to the major axis of the host galaxy. Modern deep optical surveys provide a powerful means of detecting low surface brightness (LSB) features around galaxies, which offers critical insights into the formation and evolution of galaxies with polar structures.

arxiv-2506-23882.title: An improved upper bound for the distribution of iterated Euler totient functions
arxiv-2506-23882.creator: Pei Gao, Qiyu Yang
arxiv-2506-23882.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pei Gao, Qiyu Yang. Let ϕ ⁡ ( n ) \phi(n) be the Euler totient function and ϕ k ​ ( n ) \phi_{k}(n) its k k -fold iterate. In this note, we improve the upper bound for the number of positive n ⩽ x n\leqslant x such that ϕ k + 1 ​ ( n ) ⩾ c ​ n \phi_{k+1}(n)\geqslant cn .

arxiv-2507-08260.title: Do Conversational Interfaces Limit Creativity? Exploring Visual Graph Systems for Creative Writing
arxiv-2507-08260.creator: Abhinav Sood, Maria Teresa Llano, Jon McCormack
arxiv-2507-08260.description: Abstract We present a graphical, node-based system through which users can visually chain generative AI models for creative tasks. Research in chaining LLMs has found that while chaining provides transparency, controllability and guardrails to approach certain tasks, chaining with pre-defined LLM steps prevents free exploration.

arxiv-2508-04663.title: HierarchicalPrune: Position-Aware Compression for Large-Scale Diffusion Models
arxiv-2508-04663.creator: Young D. Kwon, Rui Li, Sijia Li, Sourav Bhattacharya, Stylianos I. Venieris
arxiv-2508-04663.description: Abstract State-of-the-art text-to-image diffusion models (DMs) achieve remarkable quality, yet their massive parameter scale (8-11B) poses significant challenges for inferences on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we present HierarchicalPrune , a novel compression framework grounded in a key observation: DM blocks exhibit distinct functional hierarchies, where early blocks establish semantic structures while later blocks handle texture refinements.

pmc-10574600.title: Selectivity of Sol-Gel and Hydrothermal TiO2 Nanoparticles towards Photocatalytic Degradation of Cationic and Anionic Dyes
pmc-10574600.creator: Md. Torikul Islam, Md. Nahid Parvez Roni, Md. Yunus Ali, Md. Robiul Islam, Md. Shamim Hossan, M. Habibur Rahman, A. A. S. Mostofa Zahid, Md. Nur E Alam, Md. Abu Hanif, M. Shaheer Akhtar
pmc-10574600.description: Titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticles have been extensively studied for catalyzing the photo-degradation of organic pollutants, the photocatalyst being nonselective to the substrate. We, however, found that TiO2 nanoparticles prepared via the sol-gel and hydrothermal synthetic routes each possess a definite specificity to the charge of the substrate for photodegradation.

pmc-10727390.title: Circulating Cardiovascular Biomarkers in Cancer Therapeutics‐Related Cardiotoxicity: Review of Critical Challenges, Solutions, and Future Directions
pmc-10727390.creator: Gillian Murtagh, James L Januzzi, Marielle Scherrer‐Crosbie, Tomas G Neilan, Susan Dent, Jennifer E Ho, Vinesh Appadurai, Ray McDermott, Nausheen Akhter
pmc-10727390.description: Cardiotoxicity is a growing concern in the oncology population. Transthoracic echocardiography and multigated acquisition scans have been used for surveillance but are relatively insensitive and resource intensive. Innovative imaging techniques are constrained by cost and availability. More sensitive, cost‐effective cardiotoxicity surveillance strategies are needed. Circulating cardiovascular biomarkers could provide a sensitive, low‐cost solution.

pmc-11511150.title: Multi-Source Information-Based Bearing Fault Diagnosis Using Multi-Branch Selective Fusion Deep Residual Network
pmc-11511150.creator: Shoucong Xiong, Leping Zhang, Yingxin Yang, Hongdi Zhou, Leilei Zhang, Yolanda Vidal, Marco Carratù, Gabriele Patrizi
pmc-11511150.description: Rolling bearing is the core component of industrial machines, but it is difficult for common single signal source-based fault diagnosis methods to ensure reliable results since sensor signals are vulnerable to the pollution of background noises and the attenuation of transmitted information.

pmc-11577785.title: Microenvironment-optimized gastrodin-functionalized scaffolds orchestrate asymmetric division of recruited stem cells in endogenous bone regeneration
pmc-11577785.creator: Shilin Pan, Yao Li, Lu Wang, Yingchao Guan, Kaiyang Xv, Qing Li, Guangli Feng, Yingrui Hu, Xiaoqian Lan, Shiyi Qin, Li Gui, Limei Li
pmc-11577785.description: The regeneration of osteoporotic bone defects remains challenging as the critical stem cell function is impaired by inflammatory microenvironment. Synthetic materials that intrinsically direct osteo-differentiation versus self-renewal of recruited stem cell represent a promising alternative strategy for endogenous bone formation.

pmc-11638262.title: Multi-fidelity information fusion for turbulent transport modeling in magnetic fusion plasma
pmc-11638262.creator: Shinya Maeyama, Mitsuru Honda, Emi Narita, Shinichiro Toda
pmc-11638262.description: Maintaining the high-temperature and pressure conditions required for sustained nuclear fusion is challenging due to the turbulent transport that naturally occurs in the plasma. Developing reliable models for turbulent transport is essential for progress in fusion research and development. This study proposes multi-fidelity modeling for the improved accuracy of regression models for turbulent transport in magnetic fusion plasma.

pmc-11691362.title: WHAT DO DIRECT CARE WORKERS NEED TRAINING IN TO HELP OLDER ADULTS WITH DEMENTIA DURING MEALTIMES?
pmc-11691362.creator: Dukyoo Jung, Jisung Park, Eunju Choi, Leeho Yoo, Kahyun Kim, Seyoung Cho, Soogyung Shin
pmc-11691362.description: Older adults with dementia in long-term care facilities often encounter challenges in self-feeding owing to cognitive and physical impairments. Although direct care workers play a crucial role in facilitating meal-time activities, they lack adequate training and specific educational programs. To develop an effective program, it is essential to understand the educational needs of direct care workers providing meal assistance.

pmc-12565297.title: The Impact of an Adolescent-Friendly Approach on Metabolic Control in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes in Türkiye
pmc-12565297.creator: Ayşegül Şahiner, Ayşe Gül Güven, Zeynep Şıklar, Merih Berberoğlu, Elif Özsu, Zehra Aycan
pmc-12565297.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Metabolic control worsens in adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes. In this study, adolescent-friendly structured adolescent interviews were conducted to identify psychosocial problems. The effect of providing the necessary support for these problems on metabolic control was evaluated. Methods: In this study, a survey asking about personal, family, school, and diabetes-related information was administered face-to-face to 21 adolescents with Type 1 diabetes and poor metabolic control. At each visit, the structured adolescent interview was conducted under the headings of HEEADSSS (home/education/eating/activity/addiction/depression/safety).

pmc-12737313.title: Adaptive Kalman Filter-Based UWB Location Tracking with Optimized DS-TWR in Workshop Non-Line-of-Sight Environments
pmc-12737313.creator: Jian Wu, Yijing Xiong, Wenyang Li, Wenwei Xia
pmc-12737313.description: At the current stage, indoor Ultra-Wideband (UWB) positioning systems often encounter challenges in achieving high localization accuracy under non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions within workshop environments when employing the Double-Sided Two-Way Ranging (DS-TWR) algorithm. To address this issue, a positioning optimization method based on the DS-TWR algorithm is proposed.

pmc-13035287.title: Outpatient discharge management model: a strategy to promote continuity of care
pmc-13035287.creator: Daniele Cristina dos Reis Bobrowec, Elizabeth Bernardino, Gisele Knop Aued, Jaqueline Dias do Nascimento Selleti, Maria Manuela Ferreira Pereira da Silva Martins, Camila Rorato, Keyla Cristina da Rocha Fracarolli, Lívia Cozer Montenegro, Daniele Cristina dos Reis Bobrowec, Elizabeth Bernardino, Gise
pmc-13035287.description: Objectives:to propose an outpatient discharge management model from specialized care to primary care to promote continuity of care for chronic conditions.Methods:action research with a qualitative approach. Twenty-eight professionals, including physicians, nurses, and public administrators, participated. Data collection was carried out through participant observation, documentary research, semi-structured interviews, and workshops. The data were subjected to Creswell’s content analysis.

pmc-13273809.title: Classification of Thyroid Peroxidase (TPO) Inhibitors Using Transfer Learning with SMILES Embeddings
pmc-13273809.creator: Geven Piir, Sulev Sild, Eliana Spilioti, Dimitra Nikolopoulou, Effrosyni Katsanou, Ingrid Langezaal, Uko Maran
pmc-13273809.description: Thyroid hormones (THs) regulate many processes in mammals and, therefore, affect every organ in the body. Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) is an essential enzyme for the successful biosynthesis of THs. Although TPO inhibition is a well-documented molecular initiating event (MIE) in thyroid hormone system disruption adverse outcome pathways (AOPs), experimental methods and computational models to assess TPO activity are lacking.

pmc-13424173.title: Creatine monohydrate supplementation for recovery from muscle disuse: Timing matters
pmc-13424173.creator: Jeffrey R Stout, Patrick S Pabian
pmc-13424173.description: Creatine monohydrate supplementation is best known as an ergogenic aid. However, its potential role in recovery from muscle disuse atrophy has attracted increasing scrutiny in healthy and clinical populations. This narrative mini-review examines human studies across immobilization, reloading, orthopedic and medical rehabilitation, and exercise-induced muscle damage, with close attention to supplementation timing relative to the recovery phase.

pmc-13429655.title: Tactical and assessment competency gaps in pre-service coaches: evidence from a game-based implementation
pmc-13429655.creator: Eyup Acar, Yasin Akinci
pmc-13429655.description: This study examined tactical and assessment competency gaps in pre-service coaches within a structured game-based implementation context. An Explanatory Sequential Mixed Methods design was employed. In the quantitative phase, 40 pre-service candidates (24 Physical Education Teacher Education [PET], 16 Coach Education [CE]) were evaluated using the Educational Game Playing Skill Observation Scale, assessing preparation, implementation, and evaluation competencies.

pmc-13434482.title: Strengthening maternal nutrition counselling in the Philippines: reflections on recent evidence from Ethiopia
pmc-13434482.creator: Jessabell Cabada
pmc-13434482.description: counselling supported by visual aids and delivered by trained health workers can meaningfully influence maternal nutritional behaviours in low- and middle-income settings.
